heading: Run on a name under .localhost
body:
`ty preview --host shop.localhost` serves your app at `http://shop.localhost:3000/`. `--hostname` is another name for `--host`. `ty serve`, `ty start` and `server.host` in `server/application.json` accept the same names. A name works when it is `localhost` or ends in `.localhost`, in upper or lower case, with or without one dot at the end. Each part of the name has 1 to 63 letters, digits or hyphens. Tachyon binds `127.0.0.1` for the name without asking the operating system (RFC 6761), so the name needs no setup, and it never opens the server to the network. Another name stops with `TY1302`.

A name helps in three ways. Chrome and Firefox treat `http://shop.localhost` as a secure context, so browser APIs that need HTTPS work on plain HTTP; the Tachyon browser gate measured the same in WebKit on macOS. Cookies ignore the port, so two apps on `localhost:3000` and `localhost:3001` overwrite each other's session cookie; `shop.localhost` and `admin.localhost` keep their cookies apart. And the address says which app it is. Safari asks the operating system for the name, which works on macOS. Do not use `Domain=localhost` cookies to share a cookie between two names; keep each cookie on its own name.

A server on a loopback address answers a request only when its `Host` name is a localhost name, an IP address, the host of `tac.origin`, or a name in `server.hosts`. Any other name gets `403` with `TY1366` (see Isolation and security). When you open the app through a tunnel or a reverse proxy that sends its own name, add that name to `server.hosts`, such as `["preview.example.com", "*.tunnel.example"]`. The port is not checked, because a proxy may change it. With `--allow-non-loopback`, the server checks `Host` only when `server.hosts` is set. ADR 0094 explains the choices.
